brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 3-cell linear arrangement (pieces at 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 1,-1,0) measures 364mm x 384mm x 89mm, fits standard windowsill; uses drained bins suitable for sunny/wet conditions
Three hex-bin-full-drain bins each filled with soil and planted: basil-young in bin:0,0,0, mint-young in bin:1,0,0, parsley-young in bin:1,-1,0; visible from above in look

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell windowsill planter (364mm long) with three drained full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted with a different herb: basil, mint and parsley (young stage). Capped and bolted, verified clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three herbs for a sunny sill — I'll build your windowsill planter now.
